summary: The failure is primarily a goal-fidelity and work-granularity defect: CGKN preserved command names in the manifest but allowed a generic stage architecture to replace the requested task/Bug domain, then expanded tests far beyond the product's size. Add deterministic domain-contract and budget checks before another Provider run.
diagnosis: Manifest-level purpose text was not converted into executable domain interfaces. The promised CLI commands have no concrete handler contract, WorkItem model, repository operations, filters, sorting, or lifecycle transitions.

backend/cli.py passes a command-name string into ProjectOrchestrator, while ProjectOrchestrator.execute calls every stage. This is a direct interface contradiction that should have failed before test generation.

The test plan expanded to 19 leaves and caused 70 of 87 Provider requests even though no usable domain implementation existed. Downstream work continued after a decisive upstream goal-fidelity failure.
The generated architecture optimized for CGKN's generic import/export pipeline vocabulary instead of the explicit FocusForge product vocabulary and user flows.
provider_guidance: For an explicit CRUD CLI, freeze a domain interface before file generation: WorkItem fields and validation, JSONRepository atomic load/save/backup, WorkspaceService CRUD/filter/sort/summary/import/export methods, and one callable handler for every named command.

Reject the component plan unless each requested command maps to an implemented callable and every acceptance behavior maps to a domain method plus at least one test intent. A generic stage/orchestrator abstraction cannot satisfy this mapping by naming commands only.

Generate and validate the domain model, repository, service, and CLI in dependency order. Do not start the Tests component while a required command handler or domain behavior is absent from the published interface graph.

For a medium standard-library CLI, cap the planned implementation at eight primary source files, the test suite at five files, and total Provider requests at twelve unless a recorded complexity contract justifies more. Exceeding the cap returns NEEDS_REWORK instead of continuing paid retries.

Keep tests behavior-focused: one CRUD/lifecycle module, one query/summary module, one import/export/storage module, one CLI smoke module, and an optional corruption/error module. Do not auto-split small test modules into anchor plus three parts.
acceptance_checks: A deterministic preflight rejects a CLI manifest when add/list/show/update/move/delete/summary/export/import do not each resolve to a published callable handler.

A deterministic goal-fidelity check rejects a task/Bug workspace whose published interfaces lack the required fields, CRUD operations, filters, sorting, lifecycle states, summary, import/export modes, atomic persistence, and stable error behavior.
A medium CLI plan exceeding eight primary source files, five test files, or twelve Provider requests stops with explicit NEEDS_REWORK unless its frozen complexity contract authorizes the increase.

An offline smoke flow creates a task and bug, filters and sorts them, moves one through lifecycle states, summarizes counts, exports, imports in merge and replace modes, and verifies corruption/duplicate-ID failures without editing generated source.
Only after generated pytest and the smoke flow pass may post-build finalization proceed to local_packager and the public delivery gate.
tool_evidence_requests: Run the new manifest goal-fidelity unit tests with an injected generic-orchestrator counterexample.
Run the generated project's pytest suite with PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 and capture the canonical test receipt.
Run the complete CLI smoke flow in a temporary data directory and bind its outputs to the candidate source hash.
known_limits: This is an advisory offline diagnosis; it does not repair or validate a generated candidate.
The exact request cap may need adjustment after two comparable successful runs, but the current 87-request behavior is clearly disproportionate.
